description: Run an ordered list of labeled commands one after another, stopping at the first failure by default. Use for dependent steps (e.g. build then test then package) where order matters and a later step is pointless if an earlier one fails. Unlike batch (parallel), run_seq is sequential and short-circuits; set stopOnError=false to run every step regardless.

maxLines.description: Max stdout/stderr lines to keep per step. 0 = unlimited.

steps.description: Required. Ordered steps to run sequentially

args.description: Arguments passed directly to the binary (e.g. ['test']). With command='sh', use ['-c', '<shell script>'].

command.description: The binary to execute — NOT a shell string (e.g. 'npm', 'sh'). For pipes/redirects in a step, use command='sh' with args=['-c', '<script>'].

label.description: Label for this step in the results (defaults to the command name)

stopOnError.description: Stop at the first step with a non-zero exit code (default true).

name: run_seq

exitCode.description: 0 if every step succeeded, else the first failure's code

failedAt.description: Index of the first failing step, or null if all passed

title: Run commands in sequence
